title: Orca / Tidal - Preflight notes & config sprint
content:
Quick context:
- Customer: Tidal Media (large streaming/ML infra, AWS org). Need private deployment (VPC + dedicated capacity) for recommendation reranking and a small chat endpoint for internal ops assistants.
- Goal this sprint: get a minimal working private deployment (single availability zone) with canary routing to hosted fallback, and a documented handoff for Tidal infra team.

Main concerns/constraints (from kickoff):
- No internet egress from model infra; must route through customer NAT/proxy.
- KMS integration required for model keys. They insist on HSM-backed KMS policy.
- Peak QPS: ~120 qps for embedding service (short seq), 20 qps for chat (burst tolerant).
- SLOs: p95 latency <= 120ms for embeddings, <= 350ms for chat.

High-level plan (today -> EOD next week):
1) Preflight checklist (MUST before VPC peering):
   - [ ] Confirm AWS account IDs and role names (tidal-prod-infra, redwood-deploy-role)
   - [ ] Exchange customer CIDR ranges + allowed ports (TCP 443, 50051 internal)
   - [ ] KMS policy stub + HSM key ARN from Tidal security
   - [ ] Whitelist Redwood control-plane egress IPs in their proxy (list in Confluence link)
2) PoC deployment in customer sandbox (2 days):
   - Create 1 node pool: g5.xlarge equivalent (customer uses mixed instance types)
   - Run Redwood Private control-plane (air-gapped config) with manifests from github PR 45
   - Deploy model runner with 8-bit quantized weights for the reranker (latency test)
3) Canary + fallback routing (2 days):
   - Canary 10% traffic to Private, 90% to hosted. Monitor cost + latency.
   - Set fallback policy: if p95 > 400ms or errors > 1%, shift 100% to hosted for that route.

Quick config notes:
- Batching: embeddings workload should use small continuous batching config: target_batch_size=64, max_wait_ms=12
- KV cache: enabled for chat; cache ttl=30s for short-session reuse
- Quantization: use nf4-int8 for reranker, test perf delta vs fp16 in sandbox
- Autoscale: min_replicas=2, scale_target_qps=60 per-replica for embeddings

Commands / snippets to remember (sandbox):
- terraform workspace select tidal-sandbox || terraform workspace new tidal-sandbox
- aws sts assume-role --role-arn arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/tidal-deploy-role --role-session-name rwd-orca
- kubectl -n redwood apply -f deploy/release/private-controlplane.yaml

Initial smoke tests (to run after deploy):
- embeddings: send 1000 requests at 20 qps for 1 minute, collect p50/p95/p99
- chat: simulate 5 concurrent sessions with 3-turn dialogs, measure latency and token throughput
- cost: record GPU time and tokens to estimate hourly cost (rough calc below)

Rough cost sanity check (sandbox numbers):
- reranker: 1 GPU (g5.xlarge equiv) -> 3.2 USD/hr (baseline) * 24 * 30 = ~2300 USD/mo if single replica 24/7
- embeddings scale: target 120 qps -> likely 3 replicas at baseline -> ~6900 USD/mo (rough)
Note: present these as back-of-envelope; we'll refine after perf runs.

Open questions / blockers:
- Customer's HSM process: do they provide ephemeral keys or want Redwood to integrate long-lived key? Need security contact: "Rajesh Iyer" (asked for contact via Slack).
- Network: does their proxy allow internal TLS to hostnames (SNI) or only IPs? If only IPs, we'll need static egress list from control plane.
- Licensing: ensure model licensing doc is accepted by Tidal legal before we push quantized binaries.

Action items (owner, target date):
- Maya: collect AWS account IDs + role ARNs from Tidal (2024-11-08) [IN PROGRESS]
- Ethan: prepare terraform modules and workspace for sandbox; stub inputs in PR 45 (2024-11-09)
- Lina: draft KMS policy and send to Tidal security (2024-11-08)
- Maya/Ethan: run first perf sweep and report (2024-11-11)
- All: prepare one-page handoff doc for Tidal infra (2024-11-13)

Notes-to-self (fast):
- If p95 for embeddings spikes >200ms under continuous batching, adjust max_wait_ms down to 6 and re-run.
- Keep an eye on tokenization differences between customer input and our tokenizer; their pre-tokenization pipeline may insert zero-width chars.
- Use model-variant tag "tidal-reranker-v1-quant" for canary to avoid confusion with hosted names.

Meeting minutes (11/06 kick-off):
- Tidal: wants dedicated control plane but minimal ops overhead. Concerned about KMS/HSM and network lockdown.
- Redwood: proposed two-stage rollout (sandbox -> staged -> prod). Staging to be used for load tests only.
- Follow-ups: Tidal to provide security questionnaire answers by 11/08.

Last thoughts / heuristics:
- Don't overcommit on autoscale numbers until we have p95 perf with real-ish loads.
- Document the exact tracer ids (x-request-id) for every test to correlate with their logs.

-- end --
